events.label: birth
events.text: Born in Soest; German landscape painter.

evidence.quote: Friedrich Wilhelm Otto Modersohn ( 22 February 1865 , Soest

events.text: Began concentrating on small-scale Plein Air landscape studies, until 1889.

evidence.quote: From 1874 to 1889 , he concentrated on small-scale studies and landscapes

events.text: Began studies at the Art Academy of Düsseldorf.

evidence.quote: In 1884 , he began his studies at the Art Academy of Düsseldorf

events.text: Moved to Academy of Fine Arts Karlsruhe, studying under Hermann Baisch.

evidence.quote: Four years later , he moved to the Academy of Fine Arts , Karlsruhe , where he studied under Hermann Baisch .

events.text: First visit to Worpswede, with Fritz Mackensen.

evidence.quote: In July 1889 , he made his first visit to Worpswede with Fritz Mackensen

events.text: Worpswede group presented first group exhibition at Kunsthalle Bremen.

evidence.quote: In 1895 , they presented their first group exhibition at the Kunsthalle Bremen

events.text: Worpswede Art Colony officially established; Modersohn co-founder.

evidence.quote: In 1897 , the Art Colony was officially established and Modersohn married Helene Schröder

events.text: Married Helene Schröder, daughter of a Bremen merchant.

evidence.quote: In 1897 , the Art Colony was officially established and Modersohn married Helene Schröder

events.text: Resigned from the Art Colony association.

evidence.quote: Two years later , he resigned from the association

events.text: First wife Helene died after a long illness.

evidence.quote: The next year , his wife died after a long illness

events.text: Began illustrations and designs for Stollwerck chocolate company with Worpswede artists.

evidence.quote: Around 1900 , he and several other Worpswede artists began doing illustrations and designs for Stollwerck

events.text: Remarried Paula Becker, a well-known painter.

evidence.quote: In 1901 , he remarried

events.text: Second wife Paula Becker died of an embolism.

evidence.quote: died in 1907 , of an embolism

events.text: Moved from Worpswede to nearby Fischerhude.

evidence.quote: At that point , Modersohn felt that he could not remain in Worpswede and moved to Fischerhude

events.label: public support
events.text: Only Worpswede artist to support Kunsthalle Bremen's Van Gogh purchase.

evidence.quote: In 1911 , when the Kunsthalle Bremen purchased Van Goghs Field with Poppies , Modersohn was the only Worpswede artist to support the museum

events.text: Acquired an old farmhouse on the Gailenberg in Bad Hindelang as studio.

evidence.quote: in 1933 , he acquired an old farmhouse on the Gailenberg in Bad Hindelang

events.label: health
events.text: Became blind in right eye due to detached retina.

evidence.quote: Three years later , he became blind in his right eye , due to a detached retina

events.label: award
events.text: Awarded the Goethe Medal for Art & Science.

evidence.quote: He was awarded the Goethe Medal for Art & Science in 1940

events.text: Son Ulrich died.

evidence.quote: They had two sons , Ulrich ( 1913-1943 )

events.label: death
events.text: Died in Rotenburg.

evidence.quote: 10 March 1943 , Rotenburg

events.text: Daughter Elsbeth died.

evidence.quote: The couple had one daughter , Elsbeth ( 1898-1984 )

events.text: Daughter Mathilde Tille died.

evidence.quote: Mathilde Tille ( 1907-1998 )
